intro: We list {{published}} published MBA / PGDM colleges, from {{count}} programme listings, that are tagged as accepting ATMA. This guide to MBA colleges accepting ATMA 2026 also sets out the official 2026 test schedule published by AIMS.

ATMA is the AIMS Test for Management Admissions, a national-level test recognised by AICTE and the Ministry of Education. Official 2026 dates include 22 February, 3 May and 12 July, with a further August date published on the ATMA website.
Our first cards are in alphabetical order, not a ranking of quality. Maharashtra and Karnataka have the most tagged colleges, with large clusters in Bangalore and Pune.
listLead: These are the top MBA / PGDM colleges accepting ATMA 2026 in our records, and the first names are alphabetical. They are also the top MBA / PGDM colleges in {{place}} 2026 that we have tagged for this test.
snapshot: {{private}} of the published colleges are private, {{public}} are public, and the rest are other or untyped in our records. Bangalore, Pune, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Chennai have the most listings.
We do not hold a usable fee snapshot for this full ATMA list. Some early cards show a fee, such as AMET University at ₹3 lakh, but many others are blank.
One institute on the first page is named Acliv Technology and Management Academy (ATMA), which is a college name, not the exam body. Do not confuse the two.
firstCollegesLead: Acharya Bangalore Business School is listed with a PGDM Global Immersion card and a recorded average package of ₹6 lakh. Aditya School of Business Management, Mumbai, is listed with a PGDM fee of ₹3.90 lakh and a ₹6 lakh average.
Several first-page colleges have no recorded fee. A blank fee is missing data, not a zero-fee programme.

sections.heading: Official ATMA 2026 test format and eligibility
paragraphs: The official 2026 bulletin describes a three-hour online test with 180 questions in six sections, covering analytical reasoning, verbal skills and quantitative skills, with negative marking.

AIMS states that candidates need 50% marks in a bachelor's degree from a UGC-recognised university. Final-year students and candidates who have completed CA may also apply, as published on the official site.
bullets: The official site listed fee concessions of 25% for women candidates and 50% for candidates from notified North Eastern states, with document checks at registration.
ATMA scores are used by participating institutes for MBA, PGDM, MMS and, in some cases, MCA, subject to local university rules.
Each college still runs its own cut-off, group discussion or interview, so a test score is not an admission offer.

compare.heading: How to shortlist MBA colleges accepting ATMA 2026
paragraphs: A national test score is only one part of admission. Two colleges that both accept ATMA can differ widely in official fees, specialisations and city.

faqs.question: How many MBA colleges accepting ATMA 2026 are on this list?
faqs.answer: We list {{published}} published colleges, drawn from {{count}} programme listings, tagged for ATMA. The official participating-institute set can differ, so confirm the college on the AIMS website as well.

faqs.question: When was ATMA 2026 held?
faqs.answer: The official 2026 bulletin listed tests on 22 February, 3 May and 12 July, with a further August date published on www.atmaaims.com. Use the official site for the August date, because published notices have not always used the same August day.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for ATMA 2026?
faqs.answer: AIMS states that candidates need 50% marks in a bachelor's degree from a UGC-recognised university. Final-year students and candidates who have completed CA may also apply, as published on the official site.

faqs.question: Is ATMA recognised for MBA admissions?
faqs.answer: AIMS describes ATMA as a national-level test recognised by AICTE and the Ministry of Education for admission to MBA, PGDM and related programmes. Each college still applies its own selection rules.

faqs.question: Does an ATMA score guarantee admission?
faqs.answer: No. Institutes use the score along with their own cut-off, academic record and, often, a group discussion or interview. Confirm the latest process on the college admission page.
